messages:
alex: Hey team — quick heads up. I opened a Terraform PR to update how ExternalSecrets map to Vault paths for the payments cluster. Trying to add a stable prefix so rotation rules can target service folders instead of raw secret keys. Can folks eyeball for any policy breakage?

alex: PR: https://git.internal/redwood-inference/infra/pull/842 

alex: The change is basically this in the externalsecret CR template: 
```yaml
apiVersion: external-secrets.io/v1beta1
kind: ExternalSecret
metadata:
  name: payments-db-creds
  annotations:
    infra.redwood.com/rotation-policy: "service/payments/*"
spec:
  refreshInterval: 1m
  secretStoreRef:
    name: vault-payments
    kind: ClusterSecretStore
  target:
    name: payments-db-creds
  data:
    - secretKey: username
      remoteRef:
        key: "secret/data/services/payments/db#username"
    - secretKey: password
      remoteRef:
        key: "secret/data/services/payments/db#password"
```

maria: looks reasonable. Is the plan to rename existing Vault paths from `secret/data/payments/*` to `secret/data/services/payments/*` or to write duplicates?

alex: We want to migrate to `services/*` hierarchy. The TF change will create the new paths and update ExternalSecrets. We'll run a copy job to duplicate values for a short window and then flip readers.

noah: Heads up — if we change paths, the Vault policies bound to the payments-sa service account will need read permissions on the new path. Current policy is `path "secret/data/payments/*" { capabilities = ["read"] }`. We'll need `path "secret/data/services/payments/*" { capabilities = ["read"] }`.

jamie: Also verify the externalsecrets controller supports lookup with `secret/data/...#key` format in our controller version. We bumped controller last quarter but double-check.

alex: Good point. I'm on controller v0.6.2 in the payments cluster. I validated locally against dev Vault and the `#key` suffix works.

ryan: CI note — the terraform module that provisions the Vault policy needs an update. Something like: 
```hcl
resource "vault_policy" "payments_read" {
  name   = "payments-read"
  policy = <<EOT
path "secret/data/services/payments/*" {
  capabilities = ["read"]
}
EOT
}
```

maria: Can someone add a smoke test doc entry? I want to see exact kubectl + vault commands to confirm service can read after the flip.

alex: Added a checklist in the PR description. Quick smoke test commands: 
```bash
# from a pod with payments-sa token mounted
curl -sS --header "X-Vault-Token: $VAULT_TOKEN" \
  https://vault.internal/v1/secret/data/services/payments/db | jq .data.data
# kubectl to force refresh (externalsecrets):
kubectl annotate externalsecret payments-db-creds infra.redwood.com/force-refresh="$(date +%s)" -n payments
```

deploy-bot: Terraform plan successful for infra/terraform/vault (module.payments) — no destroy actions, 2 to add, 1 to change. :white_check_mark:

ci-bot: integration-tests/payments-secrets passed (smoke). Logs: duplication job completed, 0 failures.

noah: One more: rotation controller (our in-cluster cron) uses annotation `infra.redwood.com/rotation-policy`. Ensure the new annotation value `service/payments/*` is included in the operator config whitelist (operator-config map). If not, the rotation job will ignore them.

jamie: I'll update operator-config in the same PR so it's atomic.

maria: sounds good. once PR has updated vault_policy + operator-config + a migration plan entry i'll approve. :thumbsup:

alex: Thanks — I'll push the policy change and migration job now. ping me if smoke fails.

ryan: minor nit — can you also add a short note in #incidents runbook about how we rollback if the new paths are incomplete? quick steps to revert ExternalSecrets to the old path.

alex: will do. thanks all.

maria: Approving once CI green.

alex: CI green, merging in 10m. :rocket:
